title: Lead ranking at scale

metrics.reason: Design §4.7 gives a floor only for the roughly-10x scale ('p95 ≤ 2s per student', adopted at 10x). No owner target exists yet for 50x; tracked as info until one is set.

Diagnostic only (log-log slope of p95_ms vs scale across 1x/10x/50x, from scripts/bench/lib/prng.mjs-seeded tiles of the synthetic cohort) — 0 is flat, 1 is linear, 2 is quadratic. No target is set; it exists so a super-linear regression in rankLeadFits or its sub-scorers is VISIBLE even while the two floored p95 metrics above still pass (a jump from flat to linear can clear a generous 2s floor for a while before it stops clearing it).

notes: In-process, no database (design §4.7's 'seeded DB' fixture is replaced per this task's instruction with an in-memory tiling of the committed synthetic cohort, deterministic via scripts/bench/lib/prng.mjs). Calls the REAL rankLeadFits (src/lib/connect/matching-shared.ts), timed alone — visibleLeadsFor (the RLS-scoped-query stand-in) runs before the clock starts, since this suite measures the ranker rather than the lookup. Program-wide leads (classId null) are kept as ONE shared copy across every scale rather than tiled, so each student's visible-lead count stays roughly flat (~10 program-wide + ~10 from their own tile's class) at 1x, 10x and 50x — see the scorer's header comment for why an untiled program-wide set is load-bearing (tiling it too would grow per-student work with the SQUARE of scale, a fixture artifact indistinguishable from a real regression). The 2000ms floor on the 10x metric is design §4.7's adopted default (plan item 1, floors marked †); it is far above the measured value (typically well under 1ms per student — rankLeadFits scores a couple dozen leads with simple arithmetic) on purpose, because the property under test is 'no accidental O(students) or O(totalLeads) cost crept into the per-student path', not a tight timing target.
